title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client cancel / disconnect / reconnect & server timeouts
author: Sofia Chen
description:
Motivation:
We observed a class of issues where long-running streaming requests could leak server-side state or hold GPU KV caches after a client disconnects or when clients issue a cancel. This caused degraded throughput during load spikes and made reconnect/resume behavior ambiguous across clients and the OpenAI-compat layer.

This PR implements a coherent lifecycle for streaming connections: explicit client CANCEL handling, graceful handling of TCP/websocket disconnects with a configurable grace window, reconnect+resume semantics (sequence tokens), and server-side request/session timeouts. The changes are backward-compatible by default and gated behind runtime-configurable knobs.

Summary of changes:
- Add server-side handling for client-initiated CANCEL events (http/streaming and websocket). CANCEL triggers orderly termination of the in-flight generation and emits a final terminal event to the stream.
- Detect abrupt disconnects and start a configurable grace timeout (default 5s) during which the server retains the generation context and KV cache for potential reconnect/resume. After the grace window the session is torn down and resources freed.
- Introduce lightweight reconnect/resume protocol: clients receive a resume_token in initial stream headers and periodic checkpoints; clients can reconnect within the grace window and pass resume_token + resume_offset to continue from last consumed token. Resume is best-effort — when incompatible (model variant/rolled over) we fall back to full new generation.
- Server-side per-request idle and hard timeouts: idle_timeout (default 30s) for no client activity, and hard_timeout (default 120s) to bound total generation time. Timeouts emit structured terminal events with machine-readable reason codes for users and the OpenAI-compat layer.
- OpenAI-compat: streaming endpoints now include compatible event types for cancel/disconnect/resume and document the resume_token header. Existing clients that ignore resume tokens see no behavior changes.
- Observability: added metrics (stream.disconnects, stream.resumes, stream.cancel_count, stream.grace_evictions, stream.timeout_reasons) and tracing spans around lifecycle transitions.
- Tests: unit & integration tests for websocket and HTTP chunked streaming cancel, disconnect, reconnect, and timeout behavior. Added a new e2e test that simulates flaky network reconnections.
- Docs: API spec section describing resume_token, resume_offset, and timeout semantics. Migration notes and recommendations for SDKs.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4211)
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Integration tests for websocket + HTTP streaming
- [x] Metrics + tracing added
- [x] OpenAI-compat documentation updated
- [x] Backwards-compatible by default; feature gates for tuning

Additional notes:
- Default grace window is intentionally short (5s) to avoid holding scarce GPU KV cache resources; operators can increase if they prioritise user experience over latency/cost.
- Resume is not guaranteed for every model variant; the server will emit a resume_unavailable event with a reason when resume cannot be performed.
- We intentionally do not persist session state to durable storage; resume works only within the grace window and single-serving lifetime to avoid cross-process complexity.

Release notes:
- Streaming: add lifecycle controls for client cancel, disconnect handling with grace window, reconnect/resume with resume_token, and server timeouts (idle & hard). Backwards-compatible by default.
commits: feat(streaming): add lifecycle manager for streaming sessions
feat(streaming): implement client cancel event handling and terminal events
feat(streaming): add resume_token headers and checkpointing
perf(runtime): avoid KV cache eviction during grace window; add eviction metric
test(streaming): add e2e reconnect/resume flaky-network test
docs(api): document resume_token/resume_offset and timeout semantics
review_comments: Marcus Li: Added some nits and a question about race between grace window expiry and a reconnect arriving at the same millisecond. Can we deterministically prefer reconnect?

Sofia Chen (author): We prefer reconnect if the resume_token is valid and the resume request arrived before resource-freeing GC. Implemented a final atomic check in LifecycleManager; added a test case for the race.
Jordan Kim: Are we leaking any KV cache under high reconnect churn? Suggest metric and a limit.

Sofia Chen (author): Added stream.grace_evictions metric and a soft limit config (stream.max_resume_attempts) to avoid unbounded retries. Updated docs to recommend conservative values in multi-tenant pools.
Lina Ortega: OpenAI-compat event names look good. Please ensure SDKs expose resume_token in a first-class way.
Sofia Chen (author): Updated Python and TS SDKs to surface resume_token and provide convenience helpers; added examples in quickstarts.

Marcus Li: CI flaky e2e failed once. Re-running.
CI: e2e flaky-network failed on first run; passed on re-run.
notes_on_backward_compatibility: Defaults preserve current behavior: if clients ignore resume_token headers, streams complete or terminate as before. Resume is opt-in for clients that implement the protocol.
release_notes: Streaming: lifecycle controls — client cancel, disconnect grace window, reconnect+resume with resume_token, and server idle/hard timeouts. Metrics and SDK support added. Backwards compatible by default.
migration_instructions: SDKs should be updated to expose resume_token and resume_offset. Operators can tune defaults in runtime config: stream.grace_window_seconds, stream.idle_timeout_seconds, stream.hard_timeout_seconds. No DB migrations required.
qa_summary: Unit + integration coverage added. E2E simulated flaky networks and reconnects. Manual validation done against a staging dedicated pool with small models to ensure no KV cache leaks during churn.
post_merge_actions:
- Monitor stream.grace_evictions, stream.resumes, and stream.timeout_reasons dashboards for 2 weeks
- Add a rollout canary for Dedicated pools before enabling wider config changes
- Update external SDK release notes and examples
